newsitem.title: FRANCE: French building materials firms show solid rises.
newsitem.headline: French building materials firms show solid rises.

text.p: Building materials groups Lafarge SA and Ciments Francais posted solid gains on the Paris Bourse on Wednesday on the back of first half sales and results outlook, dealers said.
Ciments Francais was even briefly suspended limit-up, leading the gainers with a jump of more than 10 percent in the morning.
The company said on Tuesday after the market close that it expected a significant increase in its results in the second half.

Christian Duchesne of brokers EIFB said the rise in the share was justified and he upgraded his 1997 net profit forecast to 510 million francs from 480 million while he raised the 1998 outlook to 600 million from 575 million.
Muriel Felouss of SGE Delahaye also planned to raise her estimates. "The share is not expensive but far less interesting than Lafarge on fundamental reasons," she said.
Lafarge reported a 21.7 percent increase in its first half sales, which brokers Ferri called an "excellent" figure because it had expected a 6.5 percent rise.
At 1151 GMT, Ciments Francais was up 7.87 percent at 227.50 francs and Lafarge was up 3.67 percent at 435 francs.
